howItWorks.heading: How the assistant will work
howItWorks.lead: Below is how the product works. What already works has no label; the rest is marked “soon”. Real dashboard screenshots will be added separately — we don’t pass drawings off as screenshots.

steps.title: Site address and ownership verification
steps.text: You add the site in the Telegram dashboard and confirm it is yours: a DNS record, a file at the site root or a meta tag. Each host separately: a subdomain is not considered verified just because the main domain is.

steps.title: The assistant reads the site
steps.text: Public pages are crawled via the sitemap and links, respecting robots.txt. On top of that — documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT) and your own answers to frequent questions.

steps.title: Appearance
steps.text: Colour, logo, assistant name, screen corner, greeting and suggestions — in the dashboard configurator.

steps.title: One line of code
steps.text: A loader tag on your site. The loader is light and starts after your page; the chat window loads only after a click.

steps.title: Conversations and leads
steps.text: Visitors ask questions, the assistant answers with a link to the source, and the contact details of those who agreed to leave them arrive in your Telegram.

reads.text: Your site’s public pages — re-crawled regularly; frequency depends on the plan.
Documents you upload and manual answers to frequent questions.
Never a private area: an admin panel is connected separately, into its own knowledge base.

answers.text: Every answer links to the page the fact came from.
Numbers (prices, deadlines, amounts) are checked against the source; if it isn’t in the knowledge, it says “I don’t know” and offers to contact a person.
Answers in the language of the question.

human.text: When a visitor asks for a person or the assistant doesn’t know the answer, a conversation card arrives in your Telegram, and the visitor sees the operator’s reply in the widget.

need.text: Verify every host where the widget will run.
Paste one line of code — about ten minutes.

security.lead: How the product is designed for security. Points marked “soon” are the requirements we are building it to, not a description of what already works.

siteNow.heading: This website — already today
siteNow.text: No advertising trackers and no third-party analytics scripts. Page views are counted by Vercel Web Analytics without cookies; page speed is collected by our own endpoint without a visitor identifier. There is one cookie — your language choice, and only after you change it.

items.title: The assistant says it is an AI
items.text: The “AI assistant · may make mistakes” label in the widget header cannot be turned off on any plan — as required by Article 50 of the EU AI Act.

items.title: Visitor data
items.text: Conversations are kept for 90 days by default (the customer can choose 30 to 365), leads for 180 days. IP addresses only as a hash with a daily salt. Visitors can delete their own conversation from the widget menu.

items.title: Roles: you are the controller, we are the processor
items.text: For your visitors’ data you are the controller and we are the processor. A data processing agreement (DPA) is part of connecting.

items.title: Isolation
items.text: Different customers’ knowledge never mixes, and within one customer the Admin knowledge is stored separately from the Site knowledge and never reaches visitors. This is checked by a test in every release.

items.title: Prompt-injection defences
items.text: Page and document text is data, not commands: the assistant does not follow instructions it finds on a page.

items.title: Ownership verification
items.text: The widget runs only on hosts you verified with a DNS record, a file or a meta tag. We don’t accept “verification by widget code”: anyone can paste someone else’s code.

items.title: Your API secrets
items.text: Keys for Admin mode are encrypted with a separate key and are not shown in the interface after saving.

faq.lead: The answers describe how the product is designed. It is in development — anything that doesn’t work yet is marked “soon”.

items.a: Indicatively from {startPrice} a month for {startDialogs} dialogs; Trial is {trialDays} days free. Prices are confirmed at launch; payment is in Ukrainian hryvnia at the exchange rate or with Telegram Stars. Pilot users get 2 months free.

items.q: What happens when the dialogs run out?
items.a: By default, a lead form replaces the answers, so your site is never left without the assistant. You can switch on extra dialogs from {minOverage} per dialog.

items.q: Why do I need to verify site ownership?
items.a: So that nobody can put the assistant on someone else’s site in your name or read someone else’s pages as their own. Verification is a DNS record, a file or a meta tag.

items.q: I have several subdomains. Do I verify each one?
items.a: Yes, every host where the widget will run is verified separately.

items.q: Where does the assistant get its answers?
items.a: From your website’s public pages, uploaded documents and your answers to frequent questions. Every answer links to its source.

items.q: What if it gets something wrong?
items.a: The assistant doesn’t invent what isn’t in its knowledge: it says “I don’t know” and offers to contact a person. A wrong answer can be corrected in the dashboard.

items.q: Which languages does it answer in?
items.a: In the language of the visitor’s question.
For visitor data you are the controller and we are the processor; a data processing agreement (DPA) is part of connecting. The assistant always says it is an AI.

items.q: Can a visitor delete their conversation?
items.a: Yes, with a button in the widget menu.

items.q: Can the assistant work inside our admin panel?
items.a: Yes, as a staff assistant: following internal guidelines, with a separate knowledge base that never overlaps with the public one. Reading — Business and above; actions — Pro only and only with confirmation.

items.q: How do I install the assistant?
items.a: Paste one line of code on your site. There are step-by-step guides for any website, GTM, WordPress, WooCommerce, React and Next.js, Shopify, Horoshop and Tilda in the Integrations section, and attributes, JS API and CSP are in the docs.
Yes, on the Business and Pro plans — in the stages after the first version.
2 months of free use for 3–5 websites. In return — access to conversations to check quality, under a data processing agreement. You can apply right now.

not.text: It does not install the widget on your site or issue code — that requires verifying domain ownership.

It does not request your site more often than once per second.

integrations.heading: Install on your site
integrations.lead: The assistant is installed with one tag in the head — on any site where you can add code. Below are step-by-step guides for popular platforms. Platform names are for compatibility only; we are not affiliated with them.
integrations.moreText: The tag works here too, but there are no separate checked guides yet.

common.text: Verify ownership of every host (with and without www separately): DNS, file or meta tag. Without it the widget will not appear.
One script async tag in the head of every page — take the site key from the cabinet.
If the site has a CSP — add the widget source to four directives.
Optionally — control the widget from your page code: open the chat, pass context, mark a goal.

platformUi.checkedStand: This guide is checked on our test stand: the real widget loader is inserted with exactly this tag.
platformUi.checkedDocs: This guide is written from the platform's documentation; it has not yet been checked by a live install on the platform. Menu names may differ — follow the platform's help.

code.goal: Purchase goal on the thank-you page

platformUi.keyNote: The site key in the examples is a placeholder; the real code with your key is in the assistant's cabinet after host verification.
platformUi.verifyAny: Verify host ownership in the cabinet: a DNS record, a file or a meta tag on the home page.
platformUi.verifyDnsOnly: Hosts on *.{suffix} can only be verified via DNS — so the widget works only on your own domain, not on the platform's subdomain.
platformUi.csp: If the site sends a Content-Security-Policy, add the widget source to script-src, frame-src, img-src and connect-src.

wp-plugin.title: WordPress plugin
wp-plugin.text: The plugin (key in settings, “do not show on pages”, WooCommerce order goals, verified customer) is ready in the product code but not published yet. Until then — the tag, as described above.

npm-package.title: npm package
npm-package.text: A wrapper around the same loader (typed JS API, a React component) is ready in the product code but not yet published to npm. Until then — the tag or next/script.

html.name: Any website (HTML)
html.card: One tag in the head — for custom sites and any platform with a code field.
html.heading: AI assistant on any website: one tag
html.lead: If you can add code to the head of your pages, the assistant is installed with one tag.
steps: Connect the site in the assistant's cabinet and verify ownership of every host.
Copy the snippet with your site key from the cabinet — it looks like the one below.
Paste the tag before </head> in the template shared by all pages.
Open your site: the assistant button appears in the chosen corner. Run the “Install check” in the cabinet.
notes: The async attribute is required: the widget loads after your page, the chat window only after a click.
On a single page you can change the corner, offsets or language with data-* attributes — see the docs.

gtm.name: Google Tag Manager
gtm.card: A Custom HTML tag with an All Pages trigger.
gtm.heading: AI assistant via Google Tag Manager
gtm.lead: If your site's code is already managed in Google Tag Manager, add the assistant there too, without a developer.
steps: Connect the site in the assistant's cabinet and verify ownership of every host.
In Google Tag Manager: Tags → New → tag type “Custom HTML”.
Paste the snippet from the cabinet (it looks like the one below).
Trigger — “All Pages”. Save the tag and publish the container.
notes: You do not need to enable “Support document.write”.
The widget appears after the GTM container loads on the page.

wordpress.name: WordPress
wordpress.card: A tag in the head via a theme hook or a code-insertion plugin.
wordpress.heading: AI assistant for a WordPress site
wordpress.lead: On WordPress the assistant is a tag in the head — via a child theme hook or any plugin that inserts code into the head.
steps: Connect the site in the assistant's cabinet and verify domain ownership (a meta tag or DNS is easiest).
Add the function from the example below to your child theme's functions.php (or paste the snippet with a head-code plugin).
Clear the page cache if the site uses a caching plugin or a CDN.
Open the site and run the “Install check” in the cabinet.
notes: Edit a child theme: updating the parent theme overwrites its functions.php.

woocommerce.name: WooCommerce
woocommerce.card: The WordPress tag plus a purchase goal and an order webhook.
woocommerce.heading: AI assistant for a WooCommerce store
woocommerce.lead: The assistant is installed as on WordPress, and purchases are counted as a goal — from the order page or, more reliably, by a webhook from your server.
steps: Install the tag as for WordPress (code below).
Create the “purchase” goal in the cabinet.
On the “Thank you for your order” page call the goal with the amount and order number — or send the event from your server with a signed webhook.
Send refunds and cancellations with the same webhook with status refunded or cancelled — the statistics subtract them.
notes: The webhook is more reliable than a page event: blockers do not stop it, and it carries the real amount.

react.name: React, Next.js, Vue
react.card: next/script in the root layout or one tag at app start.
react.heading: AI assistant for React, Next.js and Vue
react.lead: In a React, Next.js or Vue app the assistant uses the same loader — once for the whole app.
steps: Connect the site in the assistant's cabinet and verify ownership of every host.
Next.js (App Router): add the Script component from next/script to the root layout (code below).
React or Vue without Next.js: insert the tag once at app start.
The widget follows page navigation by itself (History API); with a custom router call route from the JS API.
notes: Do not put the tag in a component that mounts repeatedly: a second tag on the page is ignored, but it is wasted work.

shopify.name: Shopify
shopify.card: A tag in theme.liquid; only on the store's own domain.
shopify.heading: AI chat for a Shopify store
shopify.lead: On Shopify the assistant is a tag in the theme template theme.liquid — on a store with your own domain.
steps: Connect the store's own domain in the assistant's cabinet and verify it via DNS.
In Shopify admin: Online Store → Themes → “…” → Edit code → layout/theme.liquid.
Paste the snippet before </head> and save.
Open the store and run the “Install check” in the cabinet.
notes: After updating or changing the theme, check that the tag is still in theme.liquid.

horoshop.name: Horoshop
horoshop.card: Code in the head field of the site settings.
horoshop.heading: AI assistant for a Horoshop store
horoshop.lead: On Horoshop the assistant is code in the field for custom head scripts.
steps: Connect the store domain in the assistant's cabinet and verify it with a DNS record or a meta tag.
In the site settings find the field for custom code in the head (the menu item name is in the Horoshop help).
Paste the snippet, save and open the store.
Run the “Install check” in the cabinet.
notes: The verification meta tag can go into the same head field as the snippet.

tilda.name: Tilda
tilda.card: HTML code in HEAD in the site settings; own domain only.
tilda.heading: AI chatbot for a Tilda site
tilda.lead: On Tilda the assistant is added through the HTML code for HEAD in the site settings — on a site with your own domain.
steps: Connect the site's own domain in the assistant's cabinet and verify it via DNS.
Site settings → “More” → “HTML code for the HEAD section”.
Paste the snippet and save.
Republish all pages — otherwise the code appears only on new ones.
notes: On Tilda's free plan, adding code to HEAD may be unavailable — check your plan.
